text: Yes, the 2022 loss was detected using Sentinel-2 imagery. The evidence shows that tree-cover loss in 2022 was observed, with a loss area of 0.6 hectares, which is 3.41% of the asset. The data source for this observation is the Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), which uses Sentinel-2 imagery among other data sources. Additionally, the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset corroborates that the area was mapped as forest in 2020, supporting the detection of loss in 2022.
